This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 03.09.2014 in M.V.C.No.487/2013 passed by the M.A.C.T. & II Addl.Senior Civil Judge, Manglaore, D.K. ('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.text: M.A.C.T. & II Addl.Senior Civil Judge, Manglaore, D.K.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, son of petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 and brother of petitioner No.3 by name Manjunath, aged 3 years, the deceased, while walking on the mud road along with petitioner No.3,
his elder NC: 2023:KHC:41299 sister, at Lingapayyakadu bus stop, hit by Innova car bearing No.KA-19/Z-8601 which came from Kolnadu side killing the deceased at the spot.
The child was declared brought dead to the Community Health Centre.
Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 being the parents and petitioner No.3 being the sister have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15 lakhs with interest @ 12% per annum.
The claim was opposed by the owner and insurer of Innova car.
After taking the evidence, the Tribunal awarded Rs.2,25,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various heads.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.B.R.Guruprasad, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.B.C.Shivanne Gowda, learned counsel for Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the Tribunal though accepted the accident awarded meager compensation globally NC: 2023:KHC:41299 without assigning any Mr Parashuram vs Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98202716/
2 reasons and sought for enhancement.

entities.text: Parashuram vs Universal Sompo General Insurance Co
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the Tribunal relying upon the judgment of the Rajasthan High Court in Sobhagya Devi and others -vs- Sukhvir Singh and Others 1 and the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Manju Devi -vs- Musafir Paswan2 has rightly awarded compensation of Rs.2,25,000/-, there is no changed circumstance for enhancement and he supported the impugned judgment.
7.

entities.text: Sobhagya Devi and others -vs- Sukhvir Singh and Others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of minor child in the accident.
The owner and the insurer have not challenged the accident by filing any appeal, thereby the finding recorded by the (2006) ACC 1997 (2005) SLT 257 NC: 2023:KHC:41299 Tribunal has reached finality.
The law has been settled that in case of death of a child, global compensation has to be awarded and this has been uniformly followed in all the cases.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kishan Gopal and another -vs- Lala and others3 has discussed in detail about the methodology for assessing compensation and awarded global compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another -vs- Lala and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was 3 years old in this case wherein in Kishan Gopal's case, the deceased was 10 years.
I do not find any distinction between the child of 3 years and 10 years.

Hence, it is proper to follow the ratio laid down in Kishan Gopal's case (supra) to award global compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- instead of Rs.2,50,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
